exact_reconciled_text: TIME_SEMANTIC and CLOCK_OR_EVIDENCE_AUTHORITY are separate governed dimensions.
FACT_OR_EFFECTIVE_TIME does not establish model-input admissibility.
PUBLIC_EVIDENCE_AVAILABLE_TIME is represented as an exact time only when governed immutable evidence supports that precision.
When governed evidence supports only a cutoff condition, preserve the existing supported_cutoff_at provenance mode and do not invent exact publication or intraday time.
Historical model/replay admissibility requires publication_at <= snapshot_cutoff_at OR supported_cutoff_at <= snapshot_cutoff_at under immutable governed provenance.
RECORDED_TIME and EXECUTION_LIFECYCLE_TIME never prove earlier historical evidence availability.
FACT_EXISTED_AT_TIME != PUBLIC_EVIDENCE_AVAILABLE_AT_TIME.

Future Outcome, MFE, MAE, Return, Rank, future High/Close, later Replay output, or later validation output shall not modify/backfill historical Snapshot, Feature, Ground Truth input, Evidence, or PIT admissibility.
Prospective scientific/business reproducibility identity references Logical Run.
Physical execution-realization evidence additionally references RunAttempt where material.
Worker, lease, claim, ACK, start, heartbeat, timeout, cancellation, retry realization, and physical runtime evidence belong to RunAttempt.
A retry may remain under the same Logical Run only when exact_execution_spec_hash is identical and governed retry policy authorizes a new RunAttempt.

Any material change to exact target, Work Order execution specification, execution profile, material dependency/lock, configuration, material input/dataset/snapshot, or execution-material model/schema identity requires a new Logical Run.
Historical T17/T18/T19 run_id and capture_run_id fields retain their original schema meaning.
Historical absence of run_attempt_id remains absence by legacy schema; synthetic historical RunAttempt generation is prohibited.
Legacy compatibility readers must label legacy Run semantics explicitly and must not silently reclassify them into Balanced-v1 Logical Run semantics.
Governed schema families bind schema_family_id, schema_version, schema_status, compatibility_with_predecessor, and reader_policy.
Frozen schema bytes are immutable; breaking semantics require a successor schema_version.
Record/data correction or snapshot revision is not a schema-version change; model version and schema version remain independent.
DECLARED_COMPATIBLE_SET must resolve to exact machine-resolvable schema identities/versions or an immutable compatible-set identity.
Floating latest, filename similarity, field-shape similarity, or presumed compatibility are prohibited.
Compatibility may be directional and shall not be presumed symmetric.
Existing MIS-v1.0, VDI-v1.0, MARM-v1.0, SIO-v1.0, and PIT interface historical semantics remain preserved unless separately superseded through governed versioning.
Governed Balanced-v1 dirty-working-tree execution is prohibited fail-closed.

Execution provenance binds stable repository identity, exact commit, git tree where material, working_tree_clean, execution profile identity/hash, dependency/lock identities, configuration hash, material inputs, applicable dataset/snapshot/model/schema identities, runtime identity, and mechanical verification evidence.
Repository identity must not depend only on a mutable display/repository name.
Exact commit alone is insufficient; commit/tree/actual checkout must be mechanically verified before governed start where material.
Material persisted inputs bind immutable identities and, where canonical/release bytes are material, available SHA256, byte size, persistent locator, and lineage.
Execution Source Provenance != Historical Evidence Provenance.
Execution timestamp, retrieval timestamp, commit identity, or clean-tree status does not establish historical evidence availability.
PIT-consumed values remain independently governed by PIT provenance and cutoff contracts.

Cross-domain references use a typed identity envelope consisting of project_namespace, entity_family_or_type, and canonical/local identity, plus revision/supersession only where the domain contract requires it.
project_namespace is a governed logical identity and is not implicitly derived from repository_full_name, branch, channel, display label, or runtime location.
Repository rename or relocation does not silently change canonical project identity.
Historical canonical IDs such as company_id, fab_id, event_id, event_record_id, run_id, and result_id are preserved exactly and are not renumbered.
The same raw string under different namespace/entity-family identities is not automatically merged.
Ambiguous cross-domain resolution and materially conflicting duplicate canonical tuples fail closed absent an explicit domain revision contract.
Version-suffix rotation shall not bypass stable identity.
The existing continuity event-ID collision is not adjudicated by R4 and remains a separate SEMI-CONTROL-ARCHITECT continuity disposition.
ACTOR_IDENTITY and AUTHORITY_IDENTITY are separate semantic dimensions.
Governed authority-bearing actions separately bind actor identity/type and authority identity/role/source/scope/exact target.
The same underlying human or Persona may legitimately appear in both dimensions for a specific action, but the actor record never substitutes for authority evidence.
Execution capability, credentials, filesystem access, CI capability, or Worker assignment do not confer governance authority.
Shared Contract promotion must resolve to dual-core reconciliation evidence and applicable promotion/Owner authority; an execution actor cannot manufacture that authority.
Independent Validation PASS does not imply Owner Freeze, Release, Live Execution, PostgreSQL Operational SoT, or Controlled Cutover.
Channel/session identity is transport context and not authority identity.
EXACT_TARGET_DECISION_RECEIPT is a standalone append-only immutable successor contract.

Minimum fields include decision_id, decision_type, target_kind, exact_target_identity, authority_ref, actor_ref if different, decision, and decided_at; rationale/prerequisite/supersedes/revokes refs are optional.
Decision values include APPROVE, DENY, REVOKE, and SUPERSEDE.

exact_target_identity must resolve to an immutable governed target or immutable compatible-version-set identity; floating latest, branch name alone, current branch HEAD alias, or mutable path alias are invalid.
APPROVAL(TARGET_X) != APPROVAL(TARGET_Y); later branch/head movement cannot expand prior authority.
Revocation or supersession creates a new receipt and preserves prior receipt bytes.
Shared Contract promotion requiring dual-core reconciliation binds the exact reconciled decision and required dual-core authority evidence.
Existing legacy approval fields remain historical evidence under their original schema and are not silently rematerialized as successor Decision Receipts.

A governed release/canonical-promotion candidate binds one immutable compatible version set identified by release_set_id, component_refs, component_set_sha256, compatibility declaration, and exact Decision Receipt reference.

Each material component reference resolves to an immutable identity/version and content hash or Git identity; persisted artifact/data components additionally bind byte size and persistent locator where applicable.

Applicable component kinds may include schema, model, feature spec, scorer/weights, model-input contract, scorer IO, execution profile, runtime source, configuration, dataset, snapshot, PIT contract, validation dataset, calendar/window mapping, Shared Contract, and model-artifact release manifest.
Floating latest is prohibited as authoritative release identity.
Individually valid components are not automatically a compatible release set; compatibility is explicitly declared or bound by an immutable compatible-set artifact.
Material changes to bound model/config/data/source/PIT/component identity create a different compatible-version-set identity and invalidate automatic reuse of validation evidence.

Existing 9/9 Shared Contract semantics and MIS-v1.0, VDI-v1.0, SIO-v1.0, MARM-v1.0, PIT, and WM-v1.1 artifacts remain preserved; prospective successors may add release_set_ref without rewriting historical bytes.
